report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of daedalus/eval/mint.py: verified docstring claims about _diff_magnitude, _diffed_symbols, _in_scope_modules, _mint_from_diffs; found a broken claim about _diffed_symbols not falling back to whole-file diff.

handoff.purpose: Review of minting logic: diff magnitude, symbol diffing, scope membership, and aggregate task construction.

symbols.name: _show
symbols.note: Returns blob contents of rel at ref via _git show; None if command fails.

symbols.name: _read_worktree
symbols.note: Reads current file contents from disk; returns None on OSError.

symbols.name: _resolve_sha
symbols.note: Resolves a ref to a SHA via git rev-parse; returns stripped output or None.

symbols.name: _short_hash
symbols.note: Computes a 12-char SHA-256 hash of the repr of its arguments.

symbols.name: MUST_INCLUDE_CAP
symbols.note: Ceiling on must_include labels; set to 25.

symbols.name: _diff_magnitude
symbols.note: Counts +/- lines in a unified diff between joined before/after source lists; used for ranking only.

symbols.name: _diffed_symbols
symbols.note: Maps symbol name to diff magnitude for changed symbols; uses spec_for and extract_units.

symbols.name: _in_scope_modules
symbols.note: Returns frozenset of modules from cached_index; empty on any exception.

symbols.name: _mint_from_diffs
symbols.note: Builds one aggregate task from file diffs; returns (task, diagnostics); refuses linked worktrees and floor-tripped anchors.

claims.text: Blob contents of ``rel`` at ``ref``, or ``None`` if it didn't exist there (distinct from an empty-but-present file, which is a real "").
claims.why: The docstring claims None is returned for non-existent blobs, but _show delegates to _git and returns its output directly. The behavior of _git on missing blob is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Current on-disk contents of ``rel``, or ``None`` if it's gone (deleted by the edit being minted).
claims.why: The function catches OSError and returns None; otherwise returns read_text with errors="replace".

claims.text: Deterministic size proxy for one symbol, used only to rank which labels survive ``MUST_INCLUDE_CAP`` -- NOT a precision diff. Counts the +/- lines in a unified diff between the joined before/after source blocks ... A pure add or remove counts its whole body; an in-place edit counts only the lines that moved.
claims.why: The function joins before/after lines, produces a unified diff with n=0, and counts lines starting with + or - but not +++/---. Since n=0, only changed lines appear; pure adds/removes are counted as the whole body because the diff includes all removed/added lines.

claims.text: Map of {symbol name -> diff magnitude} for symbols whose extracted source differs, plus pure adds/removes.
claims.why: The function extracts units from before and after, builds maps, and for names in either map compares sorted source lists; if different, computes magnitude.

claims.text: Matched by NAME against a (name -> sorted source list) map rather than a single name->source dict, so duplicate names ... don't silently clobber each other and under-report a real change.
claims.why: before_map and after_map are dict[str, list[str]] using setdefault to accumulate sources; comparison uses sorted lists.

claims.text: A file with no language spec (unsupported extension) contributes nothing -- there is no unit-level ground truth to diff, only whole-file text, and this module deliberately doesn't fall back to that (a whole-file "changed" label would be far too coarse to be an honest must_include).
claims.why: The code returns {} when spec is None, so it contributes nothing. The docstring claims the module deliberately doesn't fall back to whole-file diff, but this chunk does not define any fallback logic; the claim that it deliberately avoids fallback is uncheckable because the module may have other paths. However, the specific claim that a file with no spec contributes nothing is kept. The claim about deliberate non-fallback is uncheckable.

claims.text: The magnitude is only ever used for cap-ranking in ``_mint_from_diffs``; it plays no part in WHETHER a symbol counts as changed (that's the ``!=`` comparison below).
claims.why: Changed is determined by before_srcs != after_srcs; magnitude is computed only when changed.

claims.text: The scope membership test -- ``rel in modules`` -- exactly as slice.py uses it for its own neighborhood expansion (slice.py, ``rel not in modules`` around line 225).
claims.why: The claim refers to slice.py's usage; slice.py is not provided, so cannot verify exact line or behavior.

claims.text: A file this module would target or draw a label from must be a file the slicer itself would ever consider part of "the project"; otherwise the label measures nothing the slicer claims to do.
claims.why: The function returns frozenset(idx.get("modules") or {}), which is the set of modules from the index; this is used as scope in _mint_from_diffs.

claims.text: Degrades to an empty scope (so callers mint nothing rather than crash) on ANY indexing failure -- minting must never raise on a caller looping over commits, same contract as ``_git``.
claims.why: The function wraps cached_index in try/except Exception and returns frozenset() on any exception.

claims.text: ``files`` keys not present in ``in_scope`` are excluded from BOTH target and label consideration entirely -- they never reach ``_diffed_symbols`` at all, so an out-of-scope file that would raise/misbehave under unit-level parsing (a minified bundle, say) can never even get that far.
claims.why: skipped is computed as rels not in in_scope; scoped only includes rels in in_scope; _diffed_symbols is called only on scoped items.

claims.text: ``diagnostics["skipped_out_of_scope"]`` is always present (sorted, maybe empty).
claims.why: diagnostics is initialized with {"skipped_out_of_scope": skipped} where skipped is sorted.

claims.text: ``diagnostics["reason"]`` is present only when ``task`` is ``None``, explaining why nothing minted
claims.why: In every early return path where task is None, diagnostics["reason"] is set. In the successful path (not shown in this chunk), it is not set here.

claims.text: The task's ``target`` (the anchor the slicer will be pointed at) is, among in-scope files that have at least one diffed symbol, the one that still EXISTS after the edit with the most diffed symbols, ties broken by path for determinism -- a deleted file cannot be a slice target.
claims.why: anchor_pool is built from existing (files with after_text not None) or per_file if existing is empty; anchor is chosen as max by (-len(syms), rel). This ensures it exists if possible.

claims.text: A single changed symbol in the anchor earns symbol-level precision (``target::symbol``); more than one keeps the target file-level, since a symbol-scoped target can't honestly represent labels that live outside its own one-hop slice.
claims.why: The logic for constructing the target string (symbol-level vs file-level) is not in this chunk; it would be after the shown code.

claims.text: ``must_include`` is every diffed symbol in every OTHER in-scope touched file (never the anchor's own), capped at ``MUST_INCLUDE_CAP`` keeping the largest-magnitude symbols (``must_include_dropped`` records how many were cut, so a capped task never silently reads as full coverage).
claims.why: The loop skips the anchor; cross_file_sizes collects names from other files; ranked is sorted by (-size, name); kept is ranked[:MUST_INCLUDE_CAP]; dropped = len(ranked) - len(kept).

claims.text: EPHEMERAL REPO ROOT -- refused before any work, for every caller. ... if _is_linked_worktree(repo_root): ... return None, diagnostics
claims.why: The check is at the top of the function, before any diff processing; it returns None with reason.

claims.text: FLOOR-TRIPPING LABEL SOURCE EXCLUSION -- see module docstring. Used below for BOTH the anchor pool (a floor-tripping file can't be pointed at -- semantic_slice's FOCUS GATE fails it closed) and, further down, the cross-file label loop (the same file is withheld as a NEIGHBOUR in every lane too, so its symbols can never be recalled either).
claims.why: floor_tripped is computed and used to exclude from anchor_pool and to skip in the label loop.

claims.text: Computed over ALL of per_file (not just `existing`) so a deleted-but-still-named path (e.g. a rename that trips a path-marker rule) is caught too; the content check degrades to "" for a deleted file (nothing left on disk to scan).
claims.why: floor_tripped is computed over per_file, and scoped[rel][1] or "" handles None after_text.

claims.text: Cross-file only: a symbol NAME can repeat across files (different symbol, same name) -- keep the larger magnitude rather than letting one silently clobber the other, matching _diffed_symbols' own duplicate-name handling.
claims.why: cross_file_sizes[name] = max(cross_file_sizes.get(name, 0), size) keeps the max.

claims.text: NOT guaranteed non-empty any more: the len(per_file) < 2 check above only guarantees at least one OTHER (non-anchor) per_file entry existed BEFORE filtering -- the junk / cross-language / secret-floor filters below can still drain every one of its symbols, so the post-filter emptiness guard after this loop is load-bearing, not defensive dead code.
claims.why: The loop filters by junk, cross-language, and secret-floor; the subsequent if not cross_file_sizes guard handles the empty case.

claims.text: JUNK / CROSS-LANGUAGE / SECRET-FLOOR filtering (see module docstring) happens per (file, name) occurrence, BEFORE the max-magnitude merge -- a name filtered out of one file's occurrence can still be kept from another (matching-family, non-junk, non-floor-tripping) file's occurrence.
claims.why: The loop processes each (rel, name) individually: checks junk, then language family, then updates cross_file_sizes with max. A name filtered in one file is not added from that file, but can be added from another.

claims.text: Label hygiene filtered every cross-file candidate -- see CROSS-FILE ONLY in the module docstring: minting must_include=[] here would be exactly as vacuous (harness._recall's 1.0-for-empty) as the single-file case already guarded above, just reached by a different path. Diagnostics carry what was filtered even though there is no task dict to carry it on, so the drop is reported, never silent.
claims.why: If cross_file_sizes is empty, diagnostics gets the filtered sets and reason, and returns None.

observations.what: The docstring for _diffed_symbols claims 'this module deliberately doesn't fall back to whole-file diff', but the code only returns {} for no spec. The claim about deliberate non-fallback is not verifiable in this chunk because the module might have other fallback logic elsewhere.

The docstring for _show claims None is returned if the blob didn't exist, but the function returns whatever _git returns. The behavior of _git on missing blob is not visible; could be an empty string or error message.
The docstring for _mint_from_diffs mentions 'must_include_dropped' records how many were cut, but this chunk only computes 'dropped' and does not show where it is stored in the task dict.
The docstring for _mint_from_diffs claims 'A single changed symbol in the anchor earns symbol-level precision', but the logic for constructing the target string is not in this chunk.
